text.debian: Make sure you have the command `add-apt-repository`. It is in the package `software-properties-common` – preinstalled on Ubuntu, but not on Debian.
text.arch: Install what you need to build packages from the AUR: `git` and `base-devel`.
text.redhat: Show which repositories dnf is using right now.

hint.debian: `sudo apt update` and then `sudo apt install software-properties-common`.

text.arch: Download the build recipe for the AUR package `moonphase` to your home directory with `git clone`. The address is `https://aur.archlinux.org/moonphase.git`.

hint.debian: `sudo add-apt-repository ppa:lunatool/moonphase` – and press Enter when it asks.
hint.redhat: `sudo dnf copr enable lunatool/moonphase` – and answer `y`, No is the default.

text.debian: Look inside the file that `add-apt-repository` created in `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`.
text.arch: Read the build recipe `PKGBUILD` before you build anything!
text.redhat: List which COPR repositories have been added.

hint.debian: `ls /etc/apt/sources.list.d` and then `cat` the file whose name starts with `lunatool`.

text.debian: Install the package `moonphase` from the PPA.
text.redhat: Install the package `moonphase` from the COPR repository.

hint.debian: `add-apt-repository` already ran `apt update` for you, so `sudo apt install moonphase` is enough.
hint.arch: Stand in the directory `~/moonphase` and run `makepkg -si` – without sudo!

text.arch: List all installed packages that don't come from Arch's own repositories.
text.redhat: Find out which repository `moonphase` was installed from.

hint.redhat: `dnf info moonphase` – look at the line `From repository`.

text.debian: Remove the PPA again. The program stays, but gets no more updates.
text.arch: Bonus: install the AUR helper `yay` (the AUR package `yay-bin`) and use it to install the AUR package `snowfall`.
text.redhat: Disable the COPR repository again. The program stays, but gets no more updates.

hint.arch: Like before: `cd ~`, `git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/yay-bin.git`, `cd yay-bin` and `makepkg -si`. Then `yay -S snowfall` – without sudo.
